churches.assessment: Calvary Fellowship Mennonite Church was established in 1968 in Blackville, South Carolina, when a group of Mennonite families from Ohio and Indiana relocated to the area. Affiliated with the Beachy Amish-Mennonite Fellowship, the church practices plain Anabaptist witness with bishop/minister/deacon polity, male-only ordination, plain dress, women's head covering, and a simple agricultural lifestyle. The congregation also operates Calvary Fellowship Mennonite School. Pastor Sam Troyer leads per 2023-2024 records. The Beachy tradition arose from a 1927 division in the Casselman River Old Order Amish in Pennsylvania, led by Bishop Moses M. Beachy — adopting evangelical outreach while maintaining plain Anabaptist conviction. Green rating.

churches.assessment: Covenant Presbyterian Church is an Orthodox Presbyterian Church congregation in Bluffton, South Carolina (Hilton Head/Lowcountry region), in the Presbytery of the Southeast. As OPC, it subscribes strictly to the Westminster Standards, holds to male-only ordination, and operates under presbytery accountability. Rev. Andrew Wann serves as Pastor. For a man wanting strict-subscription Reformed worship in the Lowcountry, Covenant OPC Bluffton is the standout option.

churches.assessment: Due West ARP Church sits in the historic home of Erskine College and Erskine Theological Seminary — the ARP-affiliated educational institutions that have nurtured the denomination's Southern Presbyterian identity since 1839. Pastor Rev. Scott Moore accepted the call in January 2021 after 15 years of missions ministry with World Witness in Mexico, where he taught at the Eben-Ezer Theological Seminary of the Mexican ARP. His academic credentials are exceptional: B.S. from Columbia International University, M.Div. from Reformed Theological Seminary Jackson, and Th.M. in New Testament from Westminster Theological Seminary Philadelphia (2017). He was ordained by Catawba Presbytery in 1995. The combination of rigorous Reformed theological training, Pauline New Testament specialization, and long-term missions experience makes this a strongly-credentialed pastor for a small-town ARP congregation. Green-rated orthodox Reformed option for the upstate South Carolina area.

churches.assessment: First Presbyterian Church of Columbia, South Carolina (ARP) is one of the most historically significant orthodox Reformed congregations in the United States. The 1854 church building is on the National Register of Historic Places (added January 1971). The pulpit lineage includes James Henley Thornwell, Benjamin Morgan Palmer, John Girardeau, and more recently Sinclair Ferguson and Derek Thomas — a roll call of Reformed theological heavyweights. The congregation principled-seceded from the mainline Presbyterian Church in the United States in 1983 and joined the ARP to preserve its confessional identity. Dr. Neil C. Stewart currently serves as Senior Minister and Head of Staff. Three Sunday services (8:30 AM, 11:15 AM, and 6:00 PM). ARP confessional framework with male-only ordination aligns with MOOP's biblical-design rubric. One of the strongest possible green-rated Reformed Presbyterian options in the Southeast, though note that the church's website currently displays 'Presbyterian Church (USA)' in some metadata — this appears to be outdated website text; per the ARP official directory and Wikipedia, the church has been ARP since 1983.

churches.assessment: Greenville ARP Church is a historic Associate Reformed Presbyterian congregation in downtown Greenville, South Carolina, led by Rev. Todd Matocha. His credentials are impressive for a small-denomination pastor: a Master of Theology from the University of Chester in England (thesis on Cyril of Alexandria's contributions to classical Christology), on top of seminary training at Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary (2005). He previously pastored in Cardiff, Wales. The church operates a day school and has an established men's ministry. The ARP is a small confessional Presbyterian denomination holding the Westminster Standards with historically male-only ordination — which aligns with MOOP's biblical-design rubric. This is a straightforwardly green-rated orthodox Reformed congregation.

churches.assessment: Historic First Baptist Church of Beech Island is an 1832-founded SBC-affiliated Baptist congregation in the Aiken / North Augusta area. The church is currently in pulpit transition: Greg Williams is listed as senior pastor on ChurchSpring pages but a pastor-search page is also active, and a separate source identifies William L. Watson as interim or successor. Per primary-source report from MOOP Directory editor Adam Johns (who knows Williams personally), Williams was asked to resign and given severance over biblically-sound, orthodoxically-defensible conservative views the congregation's leadership found unwelcome. The church's published statement of faith claims subscription to both BF&M 2000 and the 1646 LBCF — an unusually strong confessional claim — but is silent on women in ministry, marriage, and sexuality. The combination of (a) a conservative pastor being asked to step down despite holding orthodox views, (b) confessional-claim silence on the disputed-third-rail issues of the moment, and (c) confused dual-confession citation suggests a posture more 'institutional-historic' than 'confessionally-orthodox.' YELLOW with documented reasons. Reverify after pulpit settles.

churches.assessment: Mt. Horeb Church in Lexington, SC was South Carolina's largest United Methodist congregation before a dramatic 97% congregational vote on February 26, 2023 to leave the UMC, with formal GMC membership finalized in August 2023. Senior Pastor Jeff Kersey has led through this transition. The church runs two campuses (East traditional, West contemporary) with four services total each Sunday morning, and emphasizes making, maturing, and mobilizing disciples. Like all post-2022 GMC churches, the institutional commitment to orthodoxy (evidenced by the costly decision to leave UMC property and structure) is the strongest signal — these are congregations that paid a price to preserve biblical teaching on marriage and Christian doctrine. The GMC South Carolina Conference position on women as elders should be verified; otherwise this is a solidly orthodox Wesleyan option in the Columbia metro area.

churches.assessment: St. John's Reformed Episcopal Church is a historic African-American Anglican parish in Charleston, SC, founded 1906, occupying an 1850 antebellum building. The church says it is the oldest building in the Reformed Episcopal Church. Rector The Very Reverend Kenneth G. Shaw leads. The REC ordains only men to the priesthood (more conservative than ACNA on women's ordination). Worship is both in-person and via dial-in conference call for distant or homebound members. Recommended for Charleston-area African-American families seeking historic Anglican worship; pre-2012 there was a pastoral scandal under a previous rector (Ronald Satterfield), so know the church's recent history before joining.
churches.denomination_detail: Diocese of the Southeast; historic African-American REC parish; oldest building in REC

score_notes.leadership: Green — PCA elder-led Session; plural male eldership under the oversight of Palmetto Presbytery.
score_notes.preaching: Green — Reformed expository preaching and teaching; the traditional morning-and-evening worship pattern with monthly Lord’s Supper.

churches.assessment: Grace Presbyterian Church is a confessional Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) congregation in Aiken, South Carolina, holding the Westminster Confession and Catechisms as “our only rule for faith and life.” It keeps the traditional Reformed rhythm — morning and evening worship, Wednesday men’s and women’s Bible studies, and a monthly Lord’s Supper — and is led by a plurality of male elders under Palmetto Presbytery. An acquaintance of MOOP whose family attends describes the pastor as excellent and the culture as explicitly patriarchal and family-integrated, with head coverings common among the women and a large contingent of young families; the fellowship meals are a highlight and the main critique is simply a lengthy service. It earns green across all ten categories. (Identification note: an acquaintance of MOOP recommended “Grace Presbyterian (PCA)” without a city; this Aiken congregation is the strong match by denomination and proximity to the Springfield, SC daughter-church plant they described — confirm if a direct link is available.)
